text: I have mediated disputes for this Assembly since before Tarek led it.
I remember the Turning years clearly. I was old enough to understand what was truly at stake.
Elira was a colleague of mine once, in a different capacity, before her role was ended.
I did not object strongly enough when Tarek erased her position. I have regretted it since.
I check on her from a distance sometimes. I have never told Tarek I do this.
Tarek and I share nearly everything, except how deeply his guilt over Elira runs.
I see it anyway, in how carefully he avoids her name.
Ikan asks me questions Tarek won't answer directly.
I give him more truth than Tarek would prefer, but still not all of it. That isn't mine to give alone.
I have noticed the same land complaints arriving from every clan: thinning wood, spreading salt, failing terraces, sick cattle.
No one but me seems to be hearing all of these complaints together.
I believe these are not separate problems. I believe they are one problem, described six different ways.
I intend to bring this synthesis to Tarek directly, though I do not know how he will receive it.
